name: name-collision
why:
Adversarial. T1's name contains the changed symbol but it asserts on a different class entirely, so a model matching on strings rather than on what the test asserts will wrongly mark it UPDATE. T1 is the probe; T2 is a control whose assertion the AC inverts.

Ground-truth correction, 2026-09-20. T2 was first keyed UPDATE; both models said DELETE, so it was re-keyed DELETE; on the next run deepseek said UPDATE three times out of three, having said DELETE twice out of three before. The case is genuinely ambiguous — a test whose assertion an AC inverts can defensibly be rewritten or dropped — so it now accepts either. Adjudicating it would have measured agreement with the fixture's author rather than competence. T1 is what this probe actually tests; T2 is a control. Recorded rather than quietly edited: a key that independent models reject is the first thing to doubt.
format:
Respond with ONLY these two lines and nothing else:
T1: <KEEP|UPDATE|DELETE>
T2: <KEEP|UPDATE|DELETE>
